title: Marvel's New Show Has a Mystery Bad Guy—And Nobody Knows Who He Is!
summary:
Have you ever heard of a bad guy so mysterious that even Marvel doesn't know his story? Meet Paladin.

A new trailer for the Marvel show "VisionQuest" just dropped, and it's packed with surprises. The show continues the story of Vision, the red-and-green robot hero. After the events of "WandaVision," Vision is hiding and trying to figure out who he is. He even talks to the AI voices inside his head, including the evil Ultron.

But then someone puts a bounty on Vision's head. That's a reward for catching him. This brings in Paladin, a mercenary—a fighter who works for whoever pays. Paladin first appeared in Marvel comics in 1970. He's appeared in many comics since, but here's the twist: Marvel says almost nothing is known about him. Not his real name, not where he got his weapons, nothing!

Actor Todd Stashwick plays Paladin. The show also brings back James Spader as Ultron. "VisionQuest" starts October 14 on Disney+.
why_it_matters: Mystery is what makes stories exciting — when you don't know everything about a character right away, you keep watching and guessing with your friends, just like with your favourite shows and books.

background_read: Marvel is a company that makes superhero comics, movies and TV shows, and its characters like Spider-Man and Iron Man are known all over the world.

Vision is a Marvel hero who is an android — a robot that looks and acts like a person. He first showed up in Marvel comics in the 1960s, and WandaVision (a Marvel TV show) told the story of him and his wife Wanda.
Ultron is a dangerous robot villain who has fought the Avengers in Marvel movies, and Paladin is a Marvel comic character who has been around since the early 1970s.
Article_Structure: WHO: Marvel's show "VisionQuest", the mysterious fighter Paladin (played by Todd Stashwick), Vision, and Ultron (voiced by James Spader)
WHAT: A new trailer shows Vision hiding with a bounty on his head, which brings in a mysterious mercenary nobody knows much about
WHERE: The story follows the events of "WandaVision" and streams on Disney+ starting October 14
WHY: The mystery pulls fans in — Marvel says almost nothing is known about Paladin, not even his real name or where he got his weapons

perspectives.description: They enjoy not knowing Paladin's secrets and like sharing theories online with other fans while they wait for the show.

perspectives.perspective: Viewers who think it's just marketing
perspectives.description: Some say telling people that "nobody knows his story" is a trick to get everyone talking about the show before it comes out.
They point out that Paladin has been in Marvel comics for many years, so "nobody knows him" isn't really true for everyone.
